items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The lowest men are unfit recipients
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To what kind of recipient may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
The chapter is the fifth
items.inference: Therefore this marks the fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: candradvīpa may be a place or textual name
items.plain_english: This is the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge
The knowledge concerns Kaula determination
The knowledge arose by another's grace
items.inference: Therefore the speaker knows the Kaula determination through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: Therefore the inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the soul dissolve, and how should this be explained fully?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is unknown
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: Therefore the teacher is asked to explain fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme attributes define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from affliction and stain
items.inference: Therefore the reality in question is defined as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is called supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also described as power and individual
items.inference: Therefore the supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: śakti+pudgalaḥ may admit more than one doctrinal reading
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where does the breath-filling vital air abide within living beings?
premises: A breath-filling air is identified
This air is situated somewhere
Its scope includes all beings
items.inference: Therefore the breath-filling vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is textually irregular
items.plain_english: The breath-filling air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The subject leaves the body
A designation is given at that moment
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Therefore upon merely leaving the body, that being is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard
It is received in the ear
It comes through traditional succession
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is heard in the ear as something transmitted through lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What transformative power is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is presented as effective
The addressee is directly addressed
items.inference: Therefore even mere heard knowledge is presented as having transformative power.
uncertainties: the result of this knowledge is completed in the following verse
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, heard and received,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner undertakes a renunciant condition
The goal is freedom from bondage
items.inference: Therefore one who practices for six months in that renunciant state becomes free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to ochre robes or a renunciant state
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months in the ochre state, free from bondage,

items.question: What benefits follow for the practitioner who completes the prescribed discipline?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
These are results of prior practice
items.inference: Therefore the disciplined practitioner becomes free from disease and joins the company of yogis.
items.plain_english: becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: A teaching has been told
The teaching concerns practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: Therefore the practice concerning the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To which kind of resolved person may this teaching be properly given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be given to a fully endowed person of firm resolve.
uncertainties: sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is doctrinally open in scope
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has firm resolve.

items.question: Under what restriction must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
This essence originates from the yoginīs
Transmission is explicitly prohibited here
items.inference: Therefore the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: the intended unfit recipient is implied rather than named
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation from ignorance to purity does the speaker claim in the present moment?
premises: The speaker refers to the present moment
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: Therefore the speaker claims a present transformation from ignorance to purity.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish concerns hearing a teaching
The teaching concerns overcoming time
items.inference: Therefore the speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious method for overcoming time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or outwitting
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed by the coming teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
No doubt is admitted
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is presented as a certain means by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you; there is no doubt, as death is destroyed.

items.question: Why can even a wise person suffer burning at the point of nectar and essence?
premises: A nectar point is involved
An essence point is involved
Even a wise person may burn
items.inference: Therefore even the wise can experience burning in relation to the nectar and essence points.
uncertainties: the physiological or yogic referents are not fully explicit
items.plain_english: Even the wise person may burn at the tip of nectar by the tip of essence.

items.question: How should the breath be drawn in at the root of tongue and palate to counteract burning?
premises: A specific bodily locus is prescribed
The breath is to be drawn in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: Therefore one should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows when this breath practice is sustained for one full year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
Old age and death are targeted
A destructive result is promised
items.inference: Therefore practicing for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protective power over poison is claimed for the accomplished practitioner’s body?
premises: Poison normally enters the body
Even bites by great serpents are considered
The poison does not enter
items.inference: Therefore the accomplished practitioner’s body is protected so that even serpent poison does not enter.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
